title: feat!: require Node.js 22 — promise the runtime we actually test (#3825)
body:
Closes the deliberately-deferred half of #3825. Follow-up to #3830.

## The promise and the evidence had stopped overlapping

Every published package declared `engines.node: ">=18.0.0"`. **Node 18 went EOL 2025-04-30 and Node 20 on 2026-04-30** — so the compatibility promise covered two runtimes nobody patches. #3830 then moved CI to Node 22, which removed the last thread connecting the promise to any evidence:

| | Node |
|---|---|
| What CI validates every PR on | **22** |
| What `release.yml` publishes from | **22** |
| What every shipped Docker image runs (`docker/Dockerfile`, `blank` template, self-hosting docs) | **22** |
| What `engines.node` promised users | **>=18** |

**No overlap at all.** We were telling users the packages support runtimes we have never once built or tested them on. #3825 correctly said this was a separate decision from the CI bump and should not be folded in — this is that decision.

`engines.node` is now `>=22.0.0` across all **50 manifests**. That is the honest floor: the only runtime these packages are built, tested and shipped on.

## Migration

**On Node 22+? Nothing changes.** Node 24 (Active LTS since 2025-10-28) and Node 26 both satisfy the range.

On Node 18 or 20 — both past end-of-life — upgrade:

```bash
nvm install 22 && nvm use 22
```

npm and pnpm surface an unsatisfied `engines` as an **`EBADENGINE` warning, not a hard failure**, so existing installs will not break the moment this lands. That is worth stating plainly *and* worth not relying on: the runtime is no longer tested, and the failures are the kind that do not announce themselves. #3812 is the worked example — a native dependency whose `engines` required a newer Node loaded anyway on the older one, then killed the vitest worker at the process level with no JS error and a summary that still read `passed`.

## Full blast radius, not just the manifests

The "Node 18+" prerequisite was restated in **ten user-facing places** — `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, four getting-started/deployment docs, the todo example, and the `objectstack-platform` skill's `compatibility` field. All now say 22. A half-done version rename is worse than none: it leaves the docs contradicting the manifest with no error anywhere.

Changelogs and ADRs are historical records and were deliberately left alone.

## Why `major` does not block anyone

Shipped as a changesets `major`. The repo is in **pre-release (`rc`) mode**, where `check-changeset-no-major` stands aside by design — accumulating breaking changes is what an RC window is *for*. Verified locally:

```
✓ Changesets is in pre-release mode (tag: rc) — `major` bumps are the expected
  product of an RC window; skipping the no-major guard.
```

Four other majors are already pending in the same window, so this is routine here rather than novel. No `allow-major` label needed.

## Verification (Node 22)

| | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm build` | ✅ 71/71, **0 cached** (the manifest edits invalidated every hash, so it genuinely rebuilt) |
| Full test suite | ✅ 129/129, **0 cached** |
| Test completeness | ✅ **16921 declared, all 16921 accounted for** — cross-checked with the guard from #3852 |
| `check-changeset-no-major` / `check-changeset-fixed` | ✅ |
| Generated skill docs / refs | ✅ in sync |

Also confirmed no test pins the old value (every `engines` assertion in the suite is about the unrelated `engines.protocol` / `engines.platform`), and that `@objectstack/client-react`'s `"react": ">=18.0.0"` peer was not caught by the sweep.
